newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly off on currency impact outlook.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly off on currency impact outlook.

text.p: Shares in Eli Lilly and Co fell 2-3/8 to 82-5/8 early Monday after the company warned industry analysts on a conference call of potential damage to 1997 earnings from currency exchange effects.
According to analysts, Lilly said on a conference call that 1997 earnings per share could be slightly under the First Call consensus of $3.19 if the dollar stays strong.
"They're talking it down to $3.15, but I'm going to stay at $3.25, which would include all events," said Rodman & Renshaw pharmaceuticals analyst James Keeney.
Analysts called the dip a buying opportunity.
"It's a little over-reaction," said Goldman Sachs analyst Prem Lachman.

Before the market opening Monday, Indianapolis-based Lilly reported earnings of $0.82 per share, excluding a $0.03 per share one-time charge. The First Call consensus had called for earnings of $0.81 per share on the quarter.
Lilly earned $0.71 per share in the year-ago quarter.

On the conference call, analysts said Lilly also talked down the future sales potential of ReoPro, a blood-clot busting drug it markets for Centocor Inc, but talked up the outlook for Zyprexa, a new anti-schizophrenia drug.
"They gave some slightly more conservative guidance than they had in the past," said Hambrecht & Quist analyst Alex Zisson.
